title: Bar Sheshakh

paragraphs: (A gentile.) Hyman relates, citing [Avodah Zarah 65a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.65a.3-4), that Rava brought Bar Sheshakh a gift on their festival, saying: “I know he does not worship idols.” He found him up to his neck in roses, with naked prostitutes before him. Bar Sheshakh asked: “Will you have anything like this in the world to come?” Rava answered: “Ours is better.” Meanwhile a royal messenger summoned him immediately to the king. As he left, he told Rava: “May the eye that wishes you harm burst!” Abaye answered “Amen,” and Bar Sheshakh’s eye burst.[^4]

notes.text: Hyman names Abaye as answering Amen; the checked Avodah Zarah passage names Rava. The supplied curse wording is damaged, but the parallel makes Bar Sheshakh the speaker wishing harm’s eye would burst, not Rava cursing his host. The final Sheshakh/Sheshach spelling variation is retained in the Hebrew.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier Avodah Zarah65a comparison has Rava answering Amen, while Hyman supplies Abaye. Bar Sheshakh wishes the eye desiring harm would burst; Rava is not made the direct curser of his host. Supplied עינא בדעי and final שישך/ששך remain unresolved. The gentile classification and complete festival/roses/royal-summons narrative are Hyman’s account, not an identified historical person.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. I, p. 293) also names Abaye, while the consulted Avodah Zarah 65a names Rava. Hyman’s print reads עינא דבעי, like the Bavli, in the curse that Bar Sheshakh addresses to Rava. It also preserves a brief line about freedom from fear of the government that is absent from the supplied Hebrew. The Bavli has a longer exchange on that point. Rashi explains בורדא as a bath of roses and takes the curse to be directed at the eye that wishes to see them harmed.

The consulted text gives Rava as the speaker who answers “Amen,” where Hyman’s print and the supplied text give Abaye. Rashi explains the setting as a [bath of roses](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.65a.3.1) and the wish as directed against the [eye that desires to see them harmed](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.65a.4.1).
